proposed_edges.uncertainty: Feed sulfur content, recovery yields, refinery retirement schedules, sulfur stocks, alternate actual output and demand all matter. Not a linear barrel-to-fertilizer rule.

payload.report:
Both sulfur and phosphate matter, at different steps. Phosphate rock supplies the phosphorus atoms plants need. Sulfur commonly supplies the acid used to free those atoms from the rock. More sulfur cannot replace missing phosphorus; potash cannot replace either nutrient.

At industrial scale, mines supply phosphate-bearing rock. Beneficiation separates useful mineral from sand, clay and other material by crushing, screening, washing and, where appropriate, flotation. The exact flowsheet depends on the deposit. Fertilizer plants commonly react prepared rock with sulfuric acid, then filter out gypsum to obtain phosphoric acid. Ammonia added to that acid produces MAP or DAP; these supply both nitrogen and phosphorus. Water circulation, grinding, acid production, filtration, waste management and transport are working capacity, not details that disappear because a mineral reserve is large. [NUT01, NUT02, NUT07]

The upstream sulfur route is itself a network. Oil refineries and sour-gas plants remove sulfur compounds; the Claus process converts hydrogen sulfide into elemental sulfur. Acid plants can use elemental sulfur, regenerated spent acid, or suitable smelter gases. These are established process families, but changing feedstocks or building a new plant is not an instant substitution. [NUT03, NUT04]

A physical constraint is already documented: Mosaic's August 27 disclosure describes Louisiana idles and Florida/Brazil curtailments, attributed to sulfur availability and affordability. This repeats and independently checks the RC-002 observation; it is not a new September shutdown. September restarts, inventory held by distributors, and missed farmer application windows remain unknown. High prices alone would not establish this; the operating disclosure is the stronger evidence. [TRS02]

Venezuela can be part of a sulfur-bearing feedstock network, conditionally. EIA identifies its crude as heavy and sour and documents dependence on diluent, specialized processing, capital and maintenance. That is historical structural context, not a September 2026 operating audit. Sulfur recovery might occur in an upgrader or refinery rather than at the oilfield. Additional oil is only additional recoverable sulfur if the receiving plant has suitable feed capacity, hydrogen/desulfurization equipment, functioning recovery units, handling and buyers. No current Venezuelan exportable sulfur surplus was established. [NUT03, NUT06]

The legal picture has changed: OFAC GL52C, effective September 14, authorizes specified PDVSA transactions by qualifying established U.S. entities subject to conditions and exclusions. Contract, payment, counterparty and vessel requirements still matter. This supports a lawful conditional pathway, not a claim of unrestricted trade or approval of any proposed sulfur transaction. [NUT05]

The UAE provides a concrete alternative node: ADNOC describes Shah's sulfur capacity as 4.2 million tons annually. That identifies industrial scale, not spare rescue stock. Its existing buyers, domestic gas requirements, actual plant availability and shipping route constrain what can be offered. Geological reserves must not be silently substituted for accessible exports. [NUT08]

An independent July IEA report identifies a common bottleneck: the Middle East supplies about one-quarter of global sulfur, while around half of seaborne sulfur trade passes through Hormuz. It reports conflict-related disruption and Chinese sulfuric-acid export curbs in May, affecting both fertilizer and mineral processing. This is dated context, not confirmation that Hormuz remains closed on September 21. The shared input exposes food and electrification supply chains to a common shock; it does not prove battery demand caused fertilizer curtailments. [NUT09]

Diesel electrification adds a useful second-order question. If cleaner transport eventually lowers refinery throughput, recovered sulfur from that throughput can fall. This is a conditional medium/long-term mechanism, not evidence that electric vehicles caused today's curtailments. The replacement program should preserve essential nutrient functions through efficiency, recovered nutrients, acid regeneration and verified alternative supply. Retaining unnecessary diesel demand is not the inferred solution. Confirmation would require linked refinery sulfur-output declines that outpace alternate supply and demand reductions; stable delivered acid/fertilizer supply would weaken the warning. [NUT03, NUT04; analytical inference]

Near-term adaptation is field-specific: soil tests can identify places where additional phosphorus provides little benefit, while protecting deficient soils. Tested manure and compost can return phosphorus, but nutrient availability, contaminants, handling and transport must be assessed. Ground rock is often a poor immediate substitute because plant availability can be low. Minnesota research supports this approach, not a universal fertilizer-cut percentage for California. [NUT07]

A commons opportunity is a grower/cooperative nutrient service: share sampling, qualified interpretation, certified input specifications and delivery coordination. Local nutrient recovery can complement commercial supply, but cannot manufacture phosphorus from nothing. Preserve donor soil fertility, existing food commitments, workers and safe plant restart capability before counting released capacity. New recovery installations and major Venezuelan rehabilitation belong in the development queue; only verified stocks and functioning contracted routes belong in today's reserve column.
